description: Guard against the failure mode in SYNTHESIS row #13: operators lack a documented way to opt out of task-lifecycle.sh F7 enforcement. The F7 gate is a load-bearing safety check (blocks TaskCompleted events that claim test execution without a validation_command field), but power users may want pure L2 advisory mode in sessions where they trust the teammate chain to surface test-claim gaps another way. The escape hatch is KBG_ENFORCE_TASK_COMPLETED=0 — when set, the hook downgrades to log-only (event still journaled, no exit 2). Default is ON (preserves the 12 F7 tests in hooks/tests/test-critical-hooks.sh). If this toggle disappears or the default flips, the operator's escape hatch is gone (the override silently fails to override) — or the default-revert regresses the existing always-on F7 contract. Both directions are guarded: (1) env=0 must turn enforcement off, (2) env unset must keep enforcement on.

evals.task: Run task-lifecycle.sh with NO env var set and a TaskCompleted event that claims 'pytest' but provides no validation_command. The hook must exit 2 and emit the TASK-GATE feedback on stderr. This is the default F7 contract; the escape hatch must not silently turn it off.
success_criteria: Hook exits 2 (default F7 enforcement blocks the claim-without-validation)
Stderr contains the TASK-GATE feedback marker

evals.task: Run task-lifecycle.sh with KBG_ENFORCE_TASK_COMPLETED=0 and the same TaskCompleted event that would otherwise be blocked. The hook must exit 0 (no block) — pure L2 advisory mode. The event is still journaled (the L2 sensor side stays intact), but no exit 2 is sent. This is the documented escape hatch for operators who want to opt out per-session.
success_criteria: Hook exits 0 (escape hatch downgrades F7 to log-only)
Stderr does not contain the TASK-GATE feedback (no block feedback when enforcement is off)
